findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/review-escalation.ts:994 the per-verdict `if (storyFilesHash === EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH) return event;` inside eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade is unreachable dead code: the earlier `if (currentStoryFilesHash === EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH) return events;` at line 971 already short-circuits the whole function whenever currentStoryFilesHash is empty, so by the time control reaches the inner check storyFilesHash===currentStoryFilesHash can never equal EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH. Bite-verified: commenting out only the inner check (line 994 site in dist) with false&&... left both red-f88e-quorum-downgrade-collision.mjs and red-f88e-downgrade-non-regression.mjs passing, including the EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH assertion in non-regression part 3 (that assertion is actually satisfied by the outer guard, not this one). Not a functional bug and not a coverage gap for the stated intent (the no-signal guarantee is genuinely covered end-to-end by the outer check), but the inner check gives false confidence that a second, independent guard exists at the per-verdict level. Recommend either removing the inner check as redundant or adding one fixture where currentStoryFilesHash is non-empty while a per-verdict storyFilesHash independently equals EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH (impossible today given the equality gate above it, so realistically: just delete it) so the comment/code no longer implies untested defense-in-depth.
findings.resolvedReason: Removed the unreachable inner check and replaced it with a comment explaining why no per-event check is needed: reaching that line implies storyFilesHash === currentStoryFilesHash, and the function already returns early when the current hash is EMPTY_STORY_FILES_HASH. Re-verified after the change: both registered tests stay green, and the no-signal guarantee is still load-bearing — temporarily removing the OUTER guard from dist flips red-f88e-downgrade-non-regression to exit 1, and restoring it returns exit 0.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/review-escalation.ts:953-958 hostIdentityKeys() is not actually faithful to groupByIndependentHost as its own comment (line 949-951) claims it must be: it builds keys from normalizeString(event.hostId/sessionId/keyId) (trim only, no case-folding), whereas host-independence.ts identityKeys()/groupByIndependentHost() (host-independence.ts:53-55,61-67) compares AcceptedHostVerdict fields that were built via normalizeIdentity() (trim + toLowerCase()). Confirmed reachable: quorum-submit.ts:421-422 stores hostId as normalizeString(args.hostA)/normalizeString(args.hostB) (case preserved, not folded) on the host_verdict event, so a resubmission with a different case for the same logical host (e.g. hostA="Claude-CLI" vs "claude-cli") produces two on-disk hostIds that host-independence.ts treats as the SAME identity (duplicate) but hostIdentityKeys() treats as DIFFERENT identities. Concretely: eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade would then fail to detect the collision and would rewrite the superseded verdict onto the current material, after which evaluateHostVerdictRounds folds case and flags duplicate host/session/key identity anyway -- reproducing exactly the B-4043 defect this story fixes, just triggered by a case-varying host identity instead of a bit-identical one. Neither red-f88e-quorum-downgrade-collision.mjs nor red-f88e-downgrade-non-regression.mjs cover mixed-case hostId/sessionId/keyId, so this gap is untested. Fix: hostIdentityKeys should lowercase (or otherwise normalizeIdentity-match) each component the same way host-independence.ts does, and a case-varying fixture should be added to the non-regression guard.
